subject: Subprocessor scope & EU residency clarification for HearthTech
messages:
From: Rachel Yang <rachel.yang@hearthtech.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.example.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@hearthtech.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jan 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Subprocessor roster + residency details request

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week — HearthTech is excited about the potential performance gains. Before legal can sign the DPA addendum, they need a current subprocessor roster and a short matrix showing which subprocessors may process EU customer data and where those subprocessors store/replicate data.

Two specific asks to speed review:
- A one-page CSV listing vendor name, service role (e.g., telemetry, CDN, KMS), primary country of processing, and whether cross-border transfer occurs.
- Confirmation whether any telemetry/observability vendors retain plaintext request bodies or model inputs.

Can you share those today or tomorrow? If it's easier, a short call with your privacy lead would be fine.

Appreciate it —
Rachel
Rachel Yang
Head of Legal Ops, HearthTech
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.example.com
To: Rachel Yang <rachel.yang@hearthtech.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@hearthtech.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 9 Jan 2028 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + residency details request

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching our current subprocessor inventory (CSV) which includes vendor role, primary processing region, and documented cross-border flows. High level answers to your two bullets:
- CSV attached: redwood_subprocessor_inventory_2028-01.csv (includes columns: vendor, service, primary_country, eu_processing_flag, stores_request_bodies)
- Observability: We do not persist plaintext request bodies for hosted requests. Telemetry captures anonymized traces and aggregated metrics; request-level telemetry that includes prompt content is disabled by default for customer-owned projects and never retained for more than 7 days in our telemetry pipeline.

Looping in Kimberly (Privacy) to confirm KMS/HSM jurisdiction details and Jonas (Infrastructure) for a note on transient telemetry retention when customers use Dedicated or Private deployments.

Next steps: Kimberly — can you confirm the KMS locations for customer keys (bring-your-own vs Redwood-managed) and whether any of the listed vendors replicate data outside the EU for hosted customers?

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
To: Rachel Yang <rachel.yang@hearthtech.com>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.example.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 10:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + residency details request

Hi Rachel / team —

Thanks for the inventory, Sergio. I reviewed the CSV and produced a short residency matrix; highlights below:
- CDN: EdgeCacheCo — primary PoPs in IE/DE/FR; CDN edge logs are pseudonymized and do not contain prompt text. For hosted customers that enable the EU region, no user content is routed outside the EU by default.
- Telemetry / Observability: StreamSight (instrumentation) processes aggregated traces in our EU telemetry cluster; raw request payloads are not stored unless a customer explicitly enables debug snapshots (opt-in, with retention controls). For HearthTech hosted account, we recommend the debug snapshots remain off.
- KMS / Encryption: For Redwood-managed keys, primary KMS is in eu-west-1 (Ireland). For BYOK customers, keys never leave the customer's KMS.
- Replication: A small set of infra health logs are replicated to our US backup region for disaster recovery; these logs do not include customer prompt text and are covered by our DPA.

I attached a redlined DPA addendum draft (dpa-addendum-draft-HT.pdf) that includes the residency commitments and an optional onshore fallback clause.

If HearthTech requires absolute in-region guarantees for all telemetry artifacts (no US backups at all), we can propose a Dedicated deployment or a Private deployment with a regional-only backup SLA — that would be a procurement conversation.

Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Yang <rachel.yang@hearthtech.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.example.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@hearthtech.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 15:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + residency details request

Kimberly — thanks, this is helpful. Two follow-ups from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether EdgeCacheCo retains TLS-terminated logs for more than 30 days? Our procurement policy flags any vendor retaining TLS-termination data beyond 30 days.
2) For the small infra logs replicated to the US for DR, can you provide an inventory of fields included so our security team can confirm there's no PII or prompt content?

If you can provide those two quick clarifications and a signed DPA addendum, we can move to countersignature. Otherwise we may need to scope a Dedicated procurement.

Best,
Rachel
From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: Rachel Yang <rachel.yang@hearthtech.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.example.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2028 15:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + residency details request

Rachel — quick answers:
- EdgeCacheCo log retention: default retention is 90 days, but EdgeCacheCo supports a 30-day retention toggle for enterprise customers. We can include the retention control in the DPA addendum language and request activation as part of onboarding.
- DR infra log fields: attached in the Drive link (see related_links) — fields are service timestamps, internal error codes, region identifiers, and hash digests of request IDs. No PII, no request text, no model inputs.

I'll update the DPA addendum to:
1) Offer the 30-day retention option for EdgeCacheCo (customer opt-in during onboarding)
2) Add an exhibit listing DR log fields and confirm no PII/model inputs are present

Sergio: once Rachel confirms, I'll circulate the updated addendum for signature (we can send as DocuSign or standard countersign).

—Marissa Cole
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
